precepts.text: The children of Israel brought pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons ordered it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever.
precepts.point: Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Samuel lay down “ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep.” Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out.

That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out. The children of Israel were to “bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always.” “Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.” Yet at a point in time it did go out.

precepts.text: Have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? In this place is one greater than the temple; and if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
precepts.point: Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: “Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning. They broke the sabbath, yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

“But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.” Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord: not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments.

precepts.text: The burnt offering of every sabbath: the priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and in the evening on the sabbath because the Lord commanded it.
precepts.point: Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot”: “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering, and his drink offering.” The priests sacrificed a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening on the sabbath, because the Lord commanded it.

That is how the priests in the temple could “profane the sabbath” and be “blameless”: the fire was kept burning and the offering made on the sabbath because it was thus saith the Lord.

precepts.text: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. This is what Christ was quoting, for the New Testament was not yet written; the knowledge of God is the keeping of the commandments.
precepts.point: Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments, he made this plain to “the house of Jacob”: “Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself. Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.”

Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning, not the blood of bulls and of goats. That is why the Lord said, “I desired mercy, and not sacrifice.”

precepts.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: your job is the training; the revealing belongs to the Most High.
precepts.point: Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Your job is the training; the revealing belongs to the Most High.

“Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.” Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord. They are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel?

You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it. Kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it. Do not rush it.

Samuel himself, in the house of the Lord from a child, “did not yet know the Lord.” Let them see you take that covenant until they are ready.

precepts.text: No man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
precepts.point: No one knows the Father until Christ reveals him, because Christ is the mediator. That is why our brothers and sisters caught up in Christianity and Islam do not know the Most High: he has not been revealed to them, and they have not been shown who they are. The word comes down in order, from the Most High to Christ, to the angels, and into our spirit when it is time to wake up; the Most High does not deal with us directly right now, because we are too full of sin.

Opening the door is repentance: put away the drugs, the whoredom, and the ways of the world, apply thus saith the Lord, and you will be full of the Lord.
precepts.point: What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:

Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” That is exactly what was read of Samuel: the word of the Lord was not yet revealed to him, and when the Lord called and he turned, saying “Speak; for thy servant heareth”, the word was made known to him.

But the other side: “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh.”

So warn your brothers and sisters of the nation of Israel: when you hear the Lord calling, through this flyer, these scriptures, this video, turn at his reproof. We do not know when he will cut a man off and leave him to his own devices to destroy himself.

Refuse to turn from the drugs, and the drugs destroy you. Refuse to stop fornicating, and the sex you love destroys you. Refuse to give up the sabbath chasing money, and money destroys you. When he cries, the Lord will not hear.

That is why, when the Lord stands and calls, you answer the first time.

precepts.text: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children: it is better to have none at all, and to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly and not be able to restrain them from doing evil.
precepts.point: Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.” “for one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly.” It is better to have none at all than to have them that are ungodly and not be able to restrain them from doing evil.

That was Eli. The Lord said, “I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.” Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not.

So the Lord swore that “the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.” When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments. His anger burns unto the lowest hell.

Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

precepts.text: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy; whether mercy reached Eli is of the Lord.
precepts.point: Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.”

“Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision”, but Eli pressed him: “I pray thee hide it not from me.” Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. “And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him.”

Eli said, “It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good.” Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli. Whether mercy reached Eli is of the Lord, and we will not know.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.
precepts.point: That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

“Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.” What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. And “all Israel from Dan even to Beer–sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.”

That is good history we read about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of us may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring our children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from. Use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

For the iniquity which he knoweth. Was Eli a wicked man doing evil stuff? No, he was not. For the iniquity, not that he did, but the iniquity that he knew.

Because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. His sons were being evil and he knew, and God told him, listen, you better check your sons. So Eli was not wicked, but he turned a blind eye toward the evil that his sons were doing. So that is the key thing you all have got to look at there. Because of what he knoweth.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. There is not going to be no offering or no sacrifice. Your life has got to pay for what you all are doing.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. He was scared to tell him what the Lord had just revealed to him.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Then Eli called Samuel, and said, Samuel, my son. And he answered, Here am I. And he said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. So he is ready to die because he did not correct his kids. He said, this is of God, just let him do it. I would have given my sons an exclusive whooping after I heard what Samuel said. You just heard from another priest, your God is about to tear your house up. So this was just crazy to me when I read it, when he already was speaking to Eli and he would not listen. Then he told Samuel, look, I am going to go and do this to him. And then Samuel was scared to tell him what he heard. The Most High will deal with men exclusively, in a place where he does not deal with somebody else the same way.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli, and the word of the Lord was precious in those days: there was no open vision.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: Three times the Lord called him and three times he ran to Eli saying, here am I, for thou calledst me, because Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. Then Eli perceived that it was the Lord calling the child and told him to answer, speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: Behold, I will do a thing in Israel at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle: in that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house, and when I begin, I will also make an end. Samuel had to carry that word to Eli, who knew exactly what evil was going on in his own house with his sons.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.

Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel?

No one knows the Father until Christ reveals him, because Christ is the mediator. That is why our brothers and sisters caught up in Christianity and Islam do not know the Most High: he has not been revealed to them, and they have not been shown who they are. The word comes down in order, from the Most High to Christ, to the angels, and into our spirit when it is time to wake up; the Most High does not deal with us directly right now, because we are too full of sin.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us.
Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end.

What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

So warn your brothers and sisters of the nation of Israel: when you hear the Lord calling, through this flyer, these scriptures, this video, turn at his reproof. We do not know when he will cut a man off and leave him to his own devices to destroy himself; and when he cries, the Lord will not hear.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him.

Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass.

That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel
